blockingFindings.failedPremise: A single branch or coder assignment does not itself reconcile a completed C1 contract slice with an incomplete combined C1/C3 implementation slice. D125 delegates freezing a completed, evidenced contract slice approved together with its freeze record. D155 authorizes only one additional final implementation slice and expressly grants no owner-policy waiver. Treating the independently completed C1 delivery as a slice leaves a subsequent C3 delivery; treating the whole combined S5 as the completion unit leaves it incomplete when C3 needs permission to start.
blockingFindings.determination: I do not approve silently redefining the completion/counting unit through a phased-branch label. D121's workflow delegation does not override D125's completion condition or D155's ticket-specific count decision. A local-proof/review pause followed by consumer coding and a final combined freeze is insufficient.
blockingFindings.boundedCorrection: Obtain the explicit Ticket140-only completion-unit/sequencing exception stated in ownerGates. Keep the proposed API and mechanism; no replacement parser, additional cache or coder-invented interface is requested. After that decision, use the precise conditional milestones below. Without it, do not assign this combined implementation.

perPdisposition.scope: Technical mechanism only, subject to B4.
perPdisposition.ruling: Reuse previously verified chain state only after validating the Reader-minted checkpoint, freshly validating the preceding-segment anchor, and hashing the exact containing-segment prefix on the same descriptor used for suffix reading.
conditions: Perform the existing option validation, directory listing, containing-segment selection, preceding last-record parsing and segment-name continuity checks before restoring state.
Match directory, colony, numeric advancing range, exact After, selected segment, version, checksum, shape and all base-chain fields.
Hash every framed byte in [0,offset), including hash text, TAB and LF, using bounded 64-KiB scratch. Do not substitute size, timestamp, a final-line hash or SameFile.
After equality, seek that same open descriptor to offset. Set absolute logical offsets and restore only the complete after-chain, with no open commit.
Preserve the fresh preceding-segment chain as the segment's base; do not accidentally replace it with the restored after-chain when capturing the next checkpoint.
Hash subsequent full lines at logical consumption, before buffer reuse. Never include bufio read-ahead beyond the completed Through boundary.
Use the existing frameLine, decodeEnvelope, lineError, verifier.accept, keep and version-checking paths for the suffix.
perPdisposition.fallback: A missing, damaged, mismatched, rotated, truncated or byte-changed hint selects ordinary scanning. In the new opener this remains checked-close mode, not a call that silently downgrades to legacy Close behavior. Genuine non-EOF I/O, seek and close failures remain errors.
perPdisposition.costLimit: Prefix I/O and SHA-256 work remain. This removes warm-prefix JSON decoding, not all prefix work, and proves no numerical bound.

perPdisposition.scope: Additive existing ledger-reader capability; completed C1 freeze still required.
perPdisposition.ruling: Use exactly the proposed opaque ReadCheckpoint, opt-in OpenReaderWithCheckpoint and Reader.Checkpoint surface. Preserve OpenReader, ReadOptions, Commit, Check and every existing consumer's legacy behavior. Do not expand ledgerstore, Receipt, privateStore or appender.
Retain one copied opaque checkpoint under the single fixed historyAckRead key in the existing LRU.

accounting.meaning: Charged retained metadata, not total RSS; bounded container/header overhead remains separately entry-bounded.

conditions: One retained-charge helper governs admission, replacement, eviction, removal and totals. Existing entries receive no additional allowance.
Copy the typed value on insertion and retrieval. Retain no Reader, descriptor, buffer, hash.Hash, commit backing storage, body bytes or pointer-bearing token payload.
Get and put require exact accepted coverage: h.through equals the requested frontier and the entry's from value. No late-fill exception.
Remove the fixed key on every accepted advance before publishing coverage, including refresh and direct-review publication.
Only successful scoped acceptance may install the newly read checkpoint at the new frontier.
Keep Service.mu before history.mu; release history.mu before I/O. Close discards the entry and reopening starts cold.

perPdisposition.ruling: Extract the existing drain into scanReader, preserving context checks, visitor/read errors and deferred Close joining. Preserve exact-one-complete-range validation and leave acceptCommitLocked unchanged.
cutover: Only the existing nonduplicate contiguous scoped-acknowledgement branch opts in.
At that private call boundary, nil means legacy reading; a nonnil zero checkpoint means an opt-in cold read.
The review caller passes nil and discards the returned proof. Its preflighted plan, witness handling and publication ordering stay unchanged.
Migrate both production callers and all four direct range-test calls without an old-signature alias.
All historical scans remain on OpenReader.
Read, exact-range validation and successful closure precede acceptance; checkpoint publication follows successful acceptance.
perPdisposition.preserved: Actual command/family/submission binding, five-family planning, duplicate-occurrence checks, schema-5 guards, reducer staging, publication, reservations, cancellation-after-durability, materialization and immutable receipt semantics remain unchanged.

perPdisposition.ruling: The private-field typed value supplies ordinary caller provenance; its checksum detects accidental damage, not malicious same-process forgery. Fresh byte identity alone never authenticates caller-asserted chain state.
minting: Only the opt-in Reader may mint a nonzero checkpoint.
Require complete numeric Through processing, terminal EOF, successful actual closure, Cursor equal to Through and verifier.done.Seq, no partial commit, and a valid final chain/logical offset.
Early Close, read failure, close failure, ToEnd and equal-bound reads issue no checkpoint.
Return a fresh value copy. No exported constructor, marshaler, unmarshaler, JSON DTO, raw-token import or caller-supplied Chain.
Directory identity uses successful Abs then Clean without alias resolution or case folding. Failure to derive that optional identity disables capture/use, not ordinary reading or checked Close.
perPdisposition.limits: The proof inherits the existing append-only live-writer protocol. It does not create a filesystem snapshot, hostile-rewrite atomicity, OS isolation or a same-process security seal.

perPdisposition.ruling: Opt-in truthful close reporting is necessary and bounded. A shared private mode is preferable to changing all legacy readers or creating a second scanner.
requiredClosureSemantics: Retain the first actual file-close failure across automatic EOF/error closure, explicit Close and repeated Close.
Stop before opening the next segment after a transition-close failure.
Apply checked closure to the preceding-segment helper and discarded candidate descriptors as well as the scanner.
Retain read errors and join actual closure failures before readCommittedRange can succeed.
Do not allow errors.Is(err, io.EOF) to erase a close failure. Normal EOF alone is not an error in a successfully drained operation.
A failed closure forbids checkpoint issuance and successful scoped acknowledgement.
Legacy OpenReader and Check retain their existing sticky Next/EOF/os.ErrClosed and Close-return semantics.

Previously completed Reader verification, fresh equality of every framed prefix byte, and equality of the freshly read predecessor chain establish those same prefix invariants. The suffix still passes the original parser/verifier. This does not interpret the prefix as exempt from verification.
verifyEveryRecord.consumption: Current Reader code skips commits at or below After before consumed-version checking. Reusing their envelope/chain proof therefore does not require reusing an old Consume map or changing version semantics. Suffix consumption and AllTypes behavior use this open's options.

ServiceProof: Warm through real successful scoped acknowledgement, then damage the earlier prefix before the next acknowledgement. Require no successful receipt, unchanged accepted projection/frontier/charge after hold release, and no successful source proof from the rejected group.
